title: PulseCare Health - Private VPC Discovery
summary: Discovery for Private VPC deployment. Discussed VPC peering vs PrivateLink, region constraints, routing, security requirements (SOC2, KMS), and next steps to share network diagram, security pack, and schedule SE-led benchmark.
next_steps: Redwood to send security pack + SOC2 and network diagram (Maya)
Customer to share current network diagram and VPC CIDRs (Priya)
Schedule SE-led networking deep dive and pilot benchmarks (Samir)
Provide initial pricing/quote for Dedicated + Private deployment (Maya)
Confirm target region and data residency requirements (Jordan)
action_items: Maya Chen: send security docs + high-level network requirements; due 2026-10-04
Priya Rao: share PulseCare VPC diagram and CIDR ranges; due 2026-10-01
Samir Patel: set up SE deep-dive and proposed benchmark plan; due 2026-10-06
Ethan Park: prepare list of required encryption/HSM controls and SSO questions; due 2026-10-02
transcript: Meeting header: 2026-09-29 15:30 PDT | Duration: 52 minutes | Attendees: Maya, Samir, Lina (Redwood); Jordan, Anita, Ethan, Priya, Marta (PulseCare)
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, we'll do quick intros and then jump into your current network setup and requirements for a private deployment.

[00:15] Jordan Reeves: Yep hi, Jordan here - CTO. Short background: we run most services in us-east-1, with a secondary region in eu-west-1 for DR. We're evaluating Redwood for internal clinical assistant features, sensitive PHI so private VPC is a requirement.
[00:32] Maya Chen: Got it. Thanks. Samir - any quick callout?
[00:35] Samir Patel: hi all. I'll focus on technical constraints, especially network egress, private endpoints and how we integrate KMS/HSM for key management.

[00:45] Anita Gomez: Quick note - we have strict egress rules. No internet-facing endpoints from our PHI subnets. Everything must be via internal peering or PrivateLink. SOC2 is mandatory, and we have customer data residency for EU patients so region matters.

[01:05] Maya Chen: Understood. At a high level, Redwood Private can run in a customer VPC with two deployment patterns: 1) VPC peering to Redwood-managed VPCs, or 2) PrivateLink / Private endpoints into your VPC. We can also do a fully private air-gapped on-prem install for extreme cases.
[01:25] Priya Rao: Can you explain practical differences? We use AWS - I'm trying to figure out which adds less ops overhead for us.

[01:32] Samir Patel: Sure. Peering is simpler for cross-VPC routing but has transitive limitations and you manage route tables. PrivateLink/Interface endpoints keep traffic on AWS backbone and are easier for fine-grained access control - each service gets an ENI in your subnet. PrivateLink is often preferred for security-conscious teams.
[01:55] Ethan Park: We need to ensure we can restrict egress entirely - i.e., no calls to public internet. Does PrivateLink allow that?

[02:02] Samir Patel: Yes. With PrivateLink + endpoint policies and restrictive route tables you can ensure traffic stays internal. Also our control plane can be configured to sit in a management VPC with limited flows, but to be clear, some metadata/ops calls might cross account depending on mode, we document exact network flows.
[02:30] Jordan Reeves: What about cross-region? Our EU patient data must remain in eu-west-1. If our users are in EU, do you run Redwood Private in eu-west-1?

[02:38] Lina Soto: We can deploy dedicated clusters in eu-west-1 for your EU workloads. The key is ensuring data residency: model inference and KV caches are in-region. Some control plane components can remain in Redwood's control plane - we can discuss a private control plane option where it's customer-managed in your account.
[02:58] Anita Gomez: Private control plane is interesting - what are the tradeoffs?

[03:02] Samir Patel: Private control plane gives you full visibility and network control but increases setup time and operational complexity on your side. We can offer a hybrid: control plane in your VPC for sensitive metadata, but Redwood-managed model serving in a dedicated VPC peered to yours. It depends on compliance needs.
[03:25] Priya Rao: For KMS, we must use our CMKs (customer-managed keys). Can Redwood integrate with our KMS or HSM?

[03:32] Samir Patel: Yes, we support customer-managed KMS keys. For Private deployments we can configure the services to call your KMS in your account or integrate with an HSM provider. There is some setup for key rotation and permissions - we'll include docs.
[03:52] Ethan Park: Audit logs - we need audit trail to go to our CloudWatch or Splunk. How does logging work?

[03:58] Lina Soto: Audit logs can be pushed to your logging endpoints via VPC flows or directly writing to S3 in your account. We provide an export connector to CloudWatch/CloudTrail. We'll share the exact schema for events.
[04:15] Jordan Reeves: Latency is also a big factor - if we host in eu-west-1 and users there, what's typical 95th latency for chat generation? We've seen numbers vary a lot on other vendors.

[04:25] Samir Patel: For a dedicated GPU pool in-region, our typical 95th token latency for a 2k context with optimized kernels is competitive; we can run a benchmark with your prompts to give you realistic numbers. That would be a next step.
[04:48] Marta Silva: Are there any special IPs or ports we need to open for PrivateLink?

[04:52] Samir Patel: The interface endpoints create ENIs in your subnet; you'll need to allow outbound TCP 443 to the endpoint IPs, and our SDK uses HTTPS. For peering, you'll need route table updates. We'll provide a 1-page checklist.
[05:10] Priya Rao: We have overlapping CIDRs across some of our VPCs - peering will be a problem. Does Redwood support Transit Gateway or PrivateLink in that case?

[05:18] Maya Chen: Yes, Transit Gateway is an option - we can peer the Redwood VPC to a TGW in your account. PrivateLink also avoids CIDR overlap issues since it uses ENIs. We'll note that in the network doc.
[05:34] Jordan Reeves: What about DNS and service discovery - can we use private DNS names for endpoints?

[05:38] Lina Soto: We support private DNS for interface endpoints, or you can configure Route53 Resolver rules if you prefer central management. We'll include DNS recommendations in the network diagram.
[05:52] Anita Gomez: On compliance: we need to see SOC2 report, pen test reports, and an architecture diagram showing data flows. Also SAML SSO for admin access. Can you provide those?
[06:02] Maya Chen: absolutely - we'll share the SOC2 Type II summary and pen test overview. We support SAML SSO and RBAC; details will be in the security pack.
[06:10] Ethan Park: Encryption in transit and at rest - confirm both?
[06:14] Samir Patel: Everything is TLS1.2+ in transit; at rest we support KMS encryption for storage and you can supply CMKs. For KV caches we can enable envelope encryption with your keys.
[06:28] Priya Rao: If we wanted an on-prem air-gapped option, what's the story?

[06:32] Samir Patel: We offer on-prem appliance installs for strict regulated customers, but that's a more involved engagement - code bundle, ops runbook, and secure transfer. Most customers prefer PrivateLink in the cloud unless policy forbids any external software.
[06:50] Jordan Reeves: Pricing - do you treat Private deployments differently?

[06:54] Maya Chen: Yes, Private and Dedicated have reserved capacity or contract pricing with monthly commitments. There are also one-time setup fees for private control planes. We'll include pricing tiers in the follow-up.
[07:06] Marta Silva: Timeline - we're hoping to run a 4-week pilot in EU for evaluation. Is that feasible?

[07:10] Samir Patel: Feasible. Typical path: 1) share network diagram and CIDRs, 2) Redwood provides network checklist & security pack, 3) SE-run benchmark/pilot in-region with your prompts, 4) evaluate, then commit to reserved capacity. We'll aim to align to your 4-week window.
[07:28] Priya Rao: Who will be our main Redwood contact for the pilot?
[07:31] Maya Chen: I'll own the commercial side, Samir will own the technical pilot. Lina will help with onboarding material. We'll loop you in for scheduling.
[07:40] Jordan Reeves: A few nitty details - do you support client IP allowlists on the endpoints and mTLS?

[07:46] Samir Patel: Endpoint policies + security groups can restrict traffic sources, and we support mTLS for mutual authentication on certain flows - we'll document the options and recommended setups.
[08:00] Anita Gomez: Any concerns about egress costs if we peer? We already pay a lot for cross-AZ traffic.

[08:06] Samir Patel: Egress depends on deployment topology. PrivateLink typically keeps traffic within AZs and can be more cost predictable. We'll include cost guidance in the proposal comparing peering vs PrivateLink and Transit Gateway patterns.
[08:24] Priya Rao: For the pilot, what logs will we get? We need request/response metadata, model version, and error traces.

[08:31] Lina Soto: We'll provide request-level telemetry, per-route latency, and token-level cost breakdown. For privacy we can redact PII in logs or have logs written to your S3 with lifecycle controls.
[08:46] Jordan Reeves: Good. Okay let's recap next steps and owners.

[08:50] Maya Chen: Recap: Maya to send security pack + SOC2, Samir to schedule and propose benchmark, Priya to send VPC diagram/CIDRs, Ethan to provide KMS/HSM and SSO requirements. We'll also send a short checklist for PrivateLink vs peering. Anything missing?
[09:06] Priya Rao: Add confirmation of target region: eu-west-1 for pilot - we'll confirm in an email.
[09:10] Jordan Reeves: We'll look for that email and try to get the network diagram by Friday.
[09:16] Maya Chen: Great - I'll follow up with docs and a calendar invite for the SE deep-dive. Thanks everyone.
[09:22] Marta Silva: thanks, bye.
[09:24] End of transcript
